# artisanvirt_vm (Resource)

A KVM virtual machine. The scheduler places it on a node in `cluster_id` (or anywhere in the fleet) unless `node_id` pins it. The API cannot resize or reconfigure an existing VM, so changes to the hardware, disks, NICs or tags replace it. `power_state` is changed in place with lifecycle actions.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "artisanvirt_vm" "web" {
  name       = "web01"
  cluster_id = artisanvirt_cluster.fsn1.id
  vcpus      = 4
  memory_mib = 8192
  firmware   = "uefi"

  disks = [
    { size_gib = 40, source_image = "/var/lib/libvirt/images/templates/rocky-10.qcow2" },
    { size_gib = 200 },
  ]

  nics = [
    { bridge = "br-lab" },
  ]

  tags = {
    role   = "web"
    backup = "nightly"
  }

  power_state = "running"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `disks` (Attributes List) Disks in order (`vda`, `vdb`, ...). All disks must use the same pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disks))
- `memory_mib` (Number) Memory in MiB.
- `name` (String) VM (libvirt domain) name, unique across the fleet.
- `vcpus` (Number)

### Optional

- `autostart` (Boolean) Start the domain when the host boots.
- `boot_iso` (String) Absolute path of an ISO on the node to boot from.
- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster to place the VM in. Empty lets the scheduler pick any cluster or standalone node.
- `cpu_mode` (String) `host-model` (default) or `host-passthrough` (less portable across CPUs).
- `delete_disks_on_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the VM's disks when it is destroyed. Defaults to `true`; set `false` to keep the disk files on the host. Backups are always kept.
- `description` (String)
- `firmware` (String) `bios` (default) or `uefi`.
- `nics` (Attributes List) Network interfaces. When omitted the VM gets one virtio NIC on the libvirt `default` network. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nics))
- `node_id` (String) Pin the VM to a node. Computed from placement when not set.
- `power_state` (String) Desired power state: `running` (default), `stopped` or `paused`. Changed in place.
- `tags` (Map of String) Tags, used for example by backup policy selectors.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_error` (String) Last task error, if any.
- `state` (String) Current VM state reported by the control plane.
- `uuid` (String) libvirt domain UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--disks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disks`

Required:

- `size_gib` (Number)

Optional:

- `pool` (String) Storage pool. Defaults to `default`.
- `source_image` (String) Absolute path of a backing image (template) on the node.

Read-Only:

- `device` (String) Guest device, e.g. `vda`.
- `path` (String) Disk path on the node.


<a id="nestedatt--nics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nics`

Optional:

- `bridge` (String) Host bridge name.
- `mac` (String) MAC address; generated when omitted.
- `model` (String)
- `network` (String) libvirt network name.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import artisanvirt_vm.web vm-0123456789abcdef
```
